They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`. 457 458 ``` 459 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true 460 ``` 461 462 Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`. 463 464 ### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`) 465 466 Each case has an expression evaluated in order. First truthy result wins; otherwise the `default` port fires. 467 468 ```json 469 { 470 "inputs": { 471 "cases": [ 472 { "label": "Low", "expression": "$vars.score <= 30" }, 473 { "label": "Medium", "expression": "$vars.score <= 70" }, 474 { "label": "High", "expression": "$vars.score > 70" } 475 ] 476 } 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ### HTTP Branch Condition (`inputs.branches[].conditionExpression`) 481 482 Uses `$self` to reference the current HTTP node's response. 483 484 ``` 485 $self.output.statusCode >= 200 && $self.output.statusCode < 300 486 ``` 487 488 ### Variable Update Expressions 489 490 Evaluate to the new value for the target variable. 491 492 ``` 493 =js:$vars.counter + 1 494 =js:$vars.items.concat([$vars.newItem.output]) 495 ``` 496 497 ### Loop Collection Expression 498 499 The `inputs.collection` field on a Loop node resolves to an array to iterate over. 500 501 ``` 502 =js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items 503 =js:$vars.inputArray.filter(x => x.active) 504 ``` 505 506 Inside the loop body, use `$vars..currentItem` and `$vars..currentIndex` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 507 508 --- 509 510 ## Jint Engine Constraints 511 512 The production runtime uses **Jint** (a .NET JavaScript interpreter, ES2020 subset). Key constraints: 513 514 ### Supported 515 516 - Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` 517 - Comparison: `===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` 518 - Logical: `&&`, `||`, `!` 519 - Ternary: `condition ? a : b` 520 - String methods: `.toUpperCase()`, `.toLowerCase()`, `.trim()`, `.split()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()`, `.slice()`, `.substring()` 521 - Array methods: `.filter()`, `.map()`, `.reduce()`, `.find()`, `.some()`, `.every()`, `.concat()`, `.length` 522 - Object: `Object.keys()`, `Object.values()`, `Object.entries()` 523 - Math: `Math.floor()`, `Math.ceil()`, `Math.round()`, `Math.abs()`, `Math.min()`, `Math.max()`, `Math.random()` 524 - JSON: `JSON.parse()`, `JSON.stringify()` 525 - Template literals: `` `Hello ${name}` `` 526 - Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` (in script bodies) 527 - Spread operator: `[...arr1, ...arr2]` (in script bodies) 528 - Arrow functions: `items.filter(x => x.active)` (inline callbacks) 529 530 ### Not Supported 531 532 - `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` — no network or timers 533 - `document`, `window`, `console` — no DOM or browser globals 534 - `require`, `import` — no module system 535 - `eval`, `Function` constructor — no dynamic code generation 536 - `async`/`await`, `Promise` — no async operations 537 - `Date` constructor may have limited support — prefer ISO 8601 strings 538 539 > **When in doubt, keep expressions simple.** Complex data processing should go in Script nodes where you have full statement support, not in one-line expressions. 540 541 --- 542 543 ## Scoping Rules 544 545 ### Node Output Availability 546 547 A node's output (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) is available to **all downstream nodes** connected via edges. If a node has not executed (e.g., on an untaken branch), its `$vars` entry is `undefined`. 548 549 ### Loop Scope 550 551 Inside a loop body, you have access to: 552 - All parent-scope `$vars` (read-only from loop's perspective) 553 - `$vars..currentItem` — current array element 554 - `$vars..currentIndex` — zero-based index 555 - `$vars..collection` — the original array 556 557 Where `` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 558 559 > **Important:** Loop body nodes must have `"parentId": ""` set in their JSON. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is inside the loop and `$vars..currentItem` will be undefined. 560 561 After loop completion, `$vars..output` contains aggregated results from all iterations. 562 563 ### Subflow Scope 564 565 Subflows have their own variable scope. Parent variables are **not** automatically visible inside a subflow. Pass values explicitly via subflow `inputs` and receive results via subflow `outputs`. 566 567 --- 568 569 ## Variable Management via CLI 570 571 There are **no CLI commands** for adding or removing variables. Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 572 573 ### Adding a workflow input variable 574 575 1. Open `.flow` 576 2. Add the variable object to `variables.globals` 577 3. 1	# Connections
2	
3	Connections are authenticated sessions for a specific connector. They store credentials and tokens, and can be shared across automations within a folder.
4	
5	> Full command syntax and options: [uip-commands.md — Integration Service](../uip-commands.md#integration-service-is). Domain-specific usage patterns are shown inline below.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Response Fields
10	
11	| Field | Show to user? | Description |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| **`Name`** | **Yes** | Display name — always use this as the primary identifier when presenting to the user (e.g., "Salesforce Prod", "bai.li") |
14	| **`State`** | **Yes** | `Enabled` or other status. Only Enabled connections can be used. |
15	| **`IsDefault`** | **Yes** | `Yes` or `No`. Recommend the default connection but always let the user confirm. |
16	| **`Owner`** | **Yes** | Who created the connection (email) |
17	| **`Folder`** | **Yes** | Folder name this connection belongs to (e.g., "Shared", "Personal") |
18	| `ConnectorName` | **Yes** | Human-readable connector name (e.g., "Slack", "Salesforce") |
19	| `ByoaConnection` | **Yes** | `Yes` or `No`. BYOA (Bring Your Own Account) connection — customer registered their own OAuth app with the external service. Required for some webhook triggers. |
20	| `Id` | Internal | Connection UUID — use only in `--connection-id` CLI args, never show to user |
21	| `ConnectorKey` | Internal | Connector key — use only in CLI args |
22	| `FolderKey` | Internal | Folder UUID — use only in `--folder-key` CLI args, never show to user |
23	| `ElementInstanceId` | Internal | Numeric instance ID — use only in `--element-instance-id` for `uip is webhooks config` |
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Command Syntax
28	
29	`<connector-key>` is a **positional argument**, not a flag:
30	
31	```bash
32	# Correct — always pass --all-folders for discovery (see Folder Scoping below)
33	uip is connections list "uipath-salesforce-slack" --all-folders --output json
34	
35	# WRONG — there is no --connector-key flag
36	uip is connections list --connector-key "uipath-salesforce-slack"
37	```
38	
39	**Always pass a connector key.** Running `uip is connections list` with no arg returns a noisy, paginated list across every connector in the tenant and is not a useful survey step.
40	
41	**Wrong key?** If the call errors with "connector not found" or returns empty unexpectedly, look up the correct key:
42	
43	```bash
44	uip is connectors list --filter "<vendor>" --output json
45	```
46	
47	Connector keys are prefixed by source — `uipath-<vendor>-<service>` for catalog connectors, `custom-entity-*` for tenant-built. See [connectors.md — Connector Disambiguation](connectors.md#connector-disambiguation) for the full classification ladder.
48	
49	---
50	
51	## Selecting a Connection
52	
53	### Connector-Specific Overrides
54	
55	**Before applying the auto-select rule below, check this table.** If the connector key (and node-type pattern, where listed) matches an entry, read the linked file and follow its rules. Override supersedes the auto-select rule.
56	
57	| Connector key | Applies when | Override action | Detail |
58	|---|---|---|---|
59	| `uipath-microsoft-teams` | `send-bot-*` activity node types | Ask user; warn that bot scope is required | [uipath-microsoft-teams.md → Connection Selection Override](connector-overrides/uipath-microsoft-teams.md#connection-selection-override) |
60	| `uipath-salesforce-slack` | Webhook trigger node types (allow-list — excludes `button-clicked`) | Ask user; filter `--byoa` from the start | [uipath-salesforce-slack.md → Connection Selection Override](connector-overrides/uipath-salesforce-slack.md#connection-selection-override) |
61	
62	To add a new override, see [connector-overrides/README.md](connector-overrides/README.md).
63	
64	---
65	
66	**Auto-select rule (no prompt) — when all three hold:**
67	
68	- `IsDefault: Yes`
69	- `State: Enabled`
70	- `Folder` is the user's personal workspace
71	
72	Bind silently and skip the presentation steps below.
73	
74	Detect the user's personal workspace once per session — list all folders and filter for the personal type:
75	
76	```bash
77	uip or folders list --all --output json
78	# → Data: [{ Name, Key, Path, Description, Type, ParentKey }]
79	# Filter entries where Type == "Personal"
80	```
81	
82	Match `connection.FolderKey` against the personal workspace's `Key`. If the call returns multiple personal workspaces (admin tenant) or no match, fall through to the presentation flow.
83	
84	**Otherwise — present connections to the user.** Recommend the default but let the user confirm.
85	
86	### Folder Scoping (`--all-folders`)
87	
88	**Always pass `--all-folders` when discovering connections.** Without it, the CLI returns the active folder only — producing false "no connections found" results when the connection exists in another folder you can see. After the user picks a connection, capture its `FolderKey` from the response for downstream binding; do not pass `--folder-key` during discovery.
89	
90	- `--all-folders`: spans every folder you have access to. Works with or without a `<connector-key>` positional.
91	- **Mutually exclusive with `--folder` / `--folder-key`** — passing both fails with `Result: Failure`, `Message: "Conflicting folder flags..."`, exit code 1.
92	
93	### For Native Connectors
94	
95	1. List connections for the connector across all folders:
96	
97	   ```bash
98	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
99	   ```
100	
101	2. Present all enabled connections to the user using **Name, Owner, and Folder** (never UUIDs), **recommending** the default (`IsDefault: Yes`, `State: Enabled`):
102	   - "I found these connections: 1) **Salesforce Prod** by user@example.com (default, enabled, Shared folder) ← recommended 2) **Salesforce Dev** by admin@example.com (enabled, Shared folder). Which should I use?"
103	3. If only one enabled connection exists, still confirm: "I found connection **<Name>** by <Owner> in **<Folder>** folder (default, enabled). Should I use this one?"
104	4. **Verify health — ping after every selection** (auto-select and user-confirmed alike):
105	
106	   ```bash
107	   uip is connections ping "<connection-id>" --output json
108	   ```
109	
110	   If ping fails or reports not Enabled, follow step 5.
111	
112	5. If not enabled (from list `State` or ping result) → prompt user to re-authenticate via `is connections edit <id>`, then re-ping.
113	
114	6. **No connections in step 1 — bypass the cache before concluding none exist:**
115	   1. Retry with `--refresh`:
116	      ```bash
117	      uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --refresh --output json
118	      ```
119	   2. If still empty, prompt user to create one via `uip is connections create "<connector-key>"`.
120	
121	### For BYOA Connections (Webhook Triggers)
122	
123	BYOA (Bring Your Own Account) connections use an OAuth app the customer registered with the external service (e.g., a Slack app they own). Some webhook triggers require BYOA; many do not. **The requirement is per event object, not per connector** — read it from the `triggers objects` response.
124	
125	**Decision flow:**
126	
127	1. Get any enabled connection — needed only as `--connection-id` for the next call:
128	
129	   ```bash
130	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
131	   ```
132	
133	2. Query trigger objects and read the `byoaConnection` flag for the matching event:
134	
135	   ```bash
136	   uip is triggers objects "<connector-key>" "<OPERATION>" \
137	     --connection-id "<id>" --output json
138	   ```
139	
140	3. **If `byoaConnection: true`** — the connection from step 1 is not usable. Filter to BYOA across all folders:
141	
142	   ```bash
143	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --byoa --all-folders --output json
144	   ```
145	
146	   If empty, retry with `--refresh` to bypass the CLI cache:
147	
148	   ```bash
149	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --byoa --all-folders --refresh --output json
150	   ```
151	
152	   If still empty, **stop and tell the user**: "This trigger requires a BYOA connection for `<connector-key>`. None found. Create one in the Integration Service portal or with `uip is connections create "<connector-key>"`, then re-run."
153	
154	4. **If `byoaConnection: false`** — use the connection from step 1. Verify health with `uip is connections ping "<id>" --output json`.
155	
156	> Connector-specific OAuth-app setup instructions (e.g., what permissions a Slack app needs) come from the trigger's `design.textBlocks` field in the `triggers objects` response. Surface that text to the user verbatim — do not invent service-specific guidance.
157	
158	For webhook URL retrieval after the trigger is configured, see [triggers.md — Webhook URL Retrieval](triggers.md#webhook-url-retrieval).
159	
160	### For HTTP Fallback
161	
162	1. List connections for `uipath-uipath-http`
163	2. Look for a connection whose **Name** contains the target vendor (case-insensitive substring match, e.g., "Apify" matches "Apify", "Apify - Prod", "My Apify Connection")
164	3. Present matches to the user. If multiple matches → let them choose.
165	4. If no match → present all existing HTTP connections and ask the user to choose, or offer to create a new one
166	
167	> **Note:** Name-based matching is best-effort. If connection names don't follow vendor naming conventions, present all HTTP connections to the user.
168	
169	---
170	
171	## Folder Scoping
172	
173	`uip is connections list <connector-key>` defaults to filtering by the **current** folder context — results from other folders (including the user's personal workspace) are silently excluded. Empty response on the filtered side looks like:
174	
175	```json
176	{"Message":"No connections found for connector '<connector-key>'."}
177	```
178	
179	even though a connection exists in another folder.
180	
181	**Cross-folder pattern** — pass `--folder` explicitly:
182	
183	```bash
184	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --folder "<folder-name-or-key>" --output json
185	```
186	
187	**Enumerate every folder** — iterate folders and list per folder:
188	
189	```bash
190	uip or folders list --output json
191	# → for each folder, call:
192	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --folder "<folder-name-or-key>" --output json
193	```
194	
195	> If the user reports "connection exists in my personal workspace but CLI can't see it", suspect default folder filtering — re-list with `--folder` set to that workspace before creating a new connection.
196	
197	---
198	
199	## Identifying a JDBC Connection's Target DB
200	
201	For the JDBC gateway connector (`uipath-uipath-jdbc`, "Database Hub"), `connections list` does **not** expose `jdbcUrl` or `driverClass` — config is intentionally hidden. The only signal for "what DB does this JDBC connection point to?" is the connection **`name`**.
202	
203	Match case-insensitively (weak signal — surface as "likely <DB>", never "is <DB>"):
204	
205	| DB | Substrings in `connection.name` |
206	|---|---|
207	| Snowflake | `snowflake`, `sf` |
208	| Databricks | `databricks`, `dbx` |
209	| Postgres | `postgres`, `postgresql`, `pg` |
210	| MySQL | `mysql` |
211	| SQL Server | `sqlserver`, `mssql` |
212	| Oracle | `oracle` |
213	| Redshift | `redshift` |
214	| BigQuery | `bigquery`, `bq` |
215	
216	If the user explicitly named a connection in their prompt (e.g. "use the `pat_databricks` connection"), that overrides name-matching — bind it directly.
217	
218	Used by the [connectors.md — JDBC Gateway](connectors.md#jdbc-gateway--database-sql-intent) decision matrix.
219	
220	---
221	
222	## Getting a Connection's Vendor Base URL
223	
224	`uip is connections base-url <connection-id>` returns the exact vendor base URL the connection uses for proxied calls (e.g., raw `http-request` calls, Managed HTTP Request in connector mode). Manual-mode invocations don't use it. The connection must be Enabled.
225	
226	```bash
227	uip is connections base-url "<connection-id>" --output json
228	# → { "Result": "Success", "Code": "ConnectionBaseUrl",
229	#     "Data": { "ConnectionId": "<id>", "BaseUrl": "https://..." } }
230	```
231	
232	Examples across connectors:
233	
234	| Connector | Returned `BaseUrl` |
235	|---|---|
236	| `uipath-atlassian-jira` | `https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/<site-id>/rest/api/2` |
237	| `uipath-microsoft-outlook365` | `https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0` |
238	| `uipath-uipath-marketo` | `https://<account>.mktorest.com/rest` |
239	
240	Use this whenever you need to compose a relative `url` for `http-request` or Managed HTTP Request in connector mode. See [http-request.md](http-request.md).
241	
242	---
243	
244	## Scope-Related Errors
245	
246	A connection can be `Enabled` but lack optional OAuth scopes needed for specific activities. This typically surfaces as a **403 Forbidden** error during execute.
247	
248	**Symptoms:**
249	- Connection pings successfully (`State: Enabled`)
250	- Execute fails with 403 or a vendor-specific "insufficient permissions" error
251	- The same operation works with a different connection that has broader scopes
252	
253	**Recovery:**
254	1. Inform the user that the connection may need broader OAuth scopes for this activity
255	2. Re-authorize with broader scopes: `uip is connections edit <connection-id>`
256	3. After re-auth, ping again to verify, then retry the operation
257

correlationId.

Decision plus two Slack nodes — do not build a large graph of switches and
per-reason handler nodes.

1. A single Script node "classify" reads the inputs and returns:
   - escalationPath:
       senderDomain empty                      -> "missing_domain"
       else customerMatchStatus == "none"      -> "unknown_customer"
       else customerMatchStatus == "multiple"  -> "multiple_matches"
       else isDuplicate is true                -> "duplicate"
       else                                    -> "escalation"
   - severity: only for "escalation" classify Sev1/Sev2/Sev3 —
       Sev1 = productionDown AND NOT workaroundAvailable;
       Sev2 = productionDown AND workaroundAvailable;
       Sev3 = NOT productionDown.

   - engineeringNeeded: true for Sev1/Sev2, otherwise false.
   - responseMode: "Draft" when escalationPath == "escalation", else "None".
